seoTitle: How to Fix an Inverted Camera on Instagram Video Calls
metaDescription: Fix a mirrored or upside-down front camera during Instagram video calls with in-app and phone-level camera settings, no third-party apps needed.
intro: A flipped or mirrored front camera during Instagram video calls can be confusing and uncomfortable to work around, but the fix is almost always a settings issue rather than a broken phone. This guide explains why Instagram shows a mirrored preview in the first place, then walks through the phone-level camera and storage settings worth checking on iPhone before you assume the app itself is broken. None of it requires installing a third-party camera app.

steps.heading: Understand why the preview looks mirrored
steps.body: Instagram deliberately shows a mirrored preview for your front camera in feeds like Reels, the same way a mirror or a laptop's built-in camera app does — it feels natural while you're framing yourself, even though the final saved video or the other person's view during a call isn't actually flipped. What looks like an inverted camera during a video call is frequently this same mirrored-preview behavior showing up somewhere it's more noticeable, rather than an actual bug in the footage being sent.

image.caption: A grid of Instagram Reels with an overlay noting that Instagram uses a mirrored preview for the front camera.

steps.heading: Check Instagram's in-app camera and call settings
steps.body: Open Instagram's settings and look through the camera and video call options for anything related to mirroring or flip behavior. Not every version of the app exposes a toggle here, but when one exists it's the fastest fix — flipping it immediately corrects how your camera displays to others without touching any phone-level settings.

steps.heading: Review your phone's system camera settings
steps.body: Open your phone's Settings app and go to the Camera section, alongside related entries like General and Control Centre. Look for any mirror-front-camera or save-as-flipped option, since some phones apply their own mirroring behavior at the operating system level that can conflict with how Instagram renders the feed during a call. Toggling this off (or on, depending on which way it's flipped) often resolves the mismatch.

image.caption: The iPhone Settings screen, with Camera listed among the system options that can affect how the front camera displays.

steps.heading: Rule out orientation and VPN conflicts
steps.body: A locked screen rotation or an active VPN can occasionally interfere with how a video call app reads your device's orientation, producing a flip that has nothing to do with Instagram's own code. Unlock rotation temporarily and disable any VPN before testing a call again, since isolating these variables narrows down whether the cause is app-side or system-side before you move on to more disruptive fixes like reinstalling.

steps.heading: Update Instagram and clear its cache
steps.body: An outdated app version is one of the most common causes of display glitches like this, so check your app store for a pending Instagram update first. If the issue persists after updating, open your phone's storage settings, find Instagram in the list of installed apps, and clear its cache or offload the app to remove corrupted local files without losing your login.

image.caption: The iPhone storage screen listing installed apps and their storage size, including Instagram — the starting point for clearing its cache.

steps.heading: Test the fix on a real call
steps.body: After making any of the changes above, start a test video call with a friend or a second device to confirm the camera now displays the right way round for both sides. Test one change at a time rather than adjusting everything at once, so if the flip returns later you know exactly which setting to revisit instead of troubleshooting from scratch.

faq.question: Why does my Instagram video call camera appear flipped?
faq.answer: It's usually because Instagram's mirrored preview behavior — normal for framing yourself in Reels and Stories — shows up during a call, combined with an app glitch, an outdated version, or a phone-level camera setting.

faq.question: Do I need a third-party app to fix a flipped camera?
faq.answer: No, this can typically be fixed using in-app settings, your phone's camera settings, and updating the app, without any extra software.

faq.question: Does this issue happen on both Android and iPhone?
faq.answer: Yes, it can occur on both platforms, though the exact menu names and settings to check differ slightly between them.

faq.question: Will clearing my cache fix the flipped camera?
faq.answer: Clearing the cache can resolve glitches contributing to the issue, especially when combined with updating the app to its latest version.

faq.question: Is the mirrored preview a bug?
faq.answer: No — Instagram mirrors the front camera preview intentionally so framing feels natural, similar to a mirror. It only becomes a problem when that mirroring carries over somewhere it shouldn't, like a live video call.
